3-3.description: An adult dragon’s lair is transforming an expanse into an environment inhospitable to the other creatures living there.

4-4.description: A long-lost journal describes an incredible journey to a hidden subterranean realm full of magical wonders.

5-5.description: Cultists hope to persuade a dragon to undergo the rite that will transform it into a dracolich.

16-16.description: A hag’s curse is making animals unusually aggressive.

17-17.description: Bullies have appointed themselves the village militia and are extorting money and food from villagers.

18-18.description: After a local fisher pulls a grotesque statue from the sea, aquatic monsters start attacking the waterfront at night.

19-19.description: The ruins on the hill near the village lie under a curse, so people don’t go there—except a scholar who wants to study the ruins.

20-20.description: A new captain has taken charge of a band of pirates or bandits and started raiding more frequently.

2-2.description: A band of giants drove away a metallic dragon and took over the dragon’s lair, and the dragon wants to reclaim the lair.

3-3.description: An ancient hero returns from the dead to prepare the world for the return of an equally ancient monster.

4-4.description: An ancient Artifact has the power to defeat or imprison a rampaging titan.

5-5.description: A god of agriculture is angry, causing rivers to dry up and crops to wither.

6-6.description: An Artifact belonging to a god falls into mortal hands.

7-7.description: A titan imprisoned in the Underdark begins to break free, causing terrible earthquakes that are only a hint of the destruction that the titan will cause if it is released.

8-8.description: A lich tries to exterminate any spellcasters that approach the lich’s level of power.

9-9.description: A holy temple was built around a portal leading to one of the Lower Planes to prevent any evil from passing through in either direction. Now the temple has come under siege from both directions.

10-10.description: Five ancient metallic dragons lair in the Pillars of Creation. If all these dragons are killed, the world will collapse into chaos. One has just been slain.

1-1.description: [[/r 5d4#Toadstools]] toadstools sprout. If a creature eats a toadstool, roll [[/r 1d2#Toadstool side-effect]]{any die}. On an odd roll, the eater must succeed on a [[/save ability=con dc=15 format=long]] or take [[/damage 5d6 type=poison]] damage and have the &Reference[Poisoned] condition for 1 hour. On an even roll, the eater gains [[/healing 5d6 type=temphp]] for 1 hour.

2-10.description: A geyser erupts and spouts water, beer, mayonnaise, tea, vinegar, wine, or oil (DM’s choice) 30 feet into the air for [[/r 1d4#Geyser duration (minutes)]] minutes.

11-20.description: A @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.actors.Actor.NB6wUgVqeOQtsQKu]{Treant} sprouts. Roll [[/r 1d2#Treant alignment]]{any die}. On an odd roll, the treant is Chaotic Evil. On an even roll, the treant is Chaotic Good.

21-30.description: An animate but immobile stone statue in your likeness rises and makes verbal threats against you. If you leave it and others come near, it describes you as the most heinous of villains and directs the newcomers to find and attack you. If you are on the same plane of existence as the statue, it knows where you are. The statue becomes inanimate after 24 hours.

31-40.description: A campfire with green flames springs forth and burns for 24 hours or until it is extinguished.

51-60.description: [[/r 1d4 + 4#Bright-pink toads]] bright-pink @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.actors.Actor.phbmobFrog000000]{toads} crawl forth. Whenever a toad is touched, it transforms into a Large or smaller monster of the DM’s choice that acts in accordance with its alignment and nature. The monster remains for 1 minute, then disappears in a puff of bright-pink smoke.

61-70.description: A hungry @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.actors.Actor.1ES45ODWg3pCrkzv]{Bulette} burrows up and attacks.

71-80.description: A fruit tree grows. It has [[/r 1d10 + 20#Pieces of fruit]] fruit, [[/gmr 1d8#Fruits acting as Potions]] of which act as randomly determined potions. The tree vanishes after 1 hour. Picked fruit remains, retaining any magic for 30 days.

81-90.description: A nest of [[/r 1d4 + 3#Rainbow-colored eggs]] rainbow-colored eggs springs up. Any creature that eats an egg makes a [[/save ability=con dc=20 format=long]]. On a successful save, a creature permanently increases its lowest ability score by 1, randomly choosing among equally low scores. On a failed save, the creature takes [[/damage 10d6 type=force]] damage from an internal explosion.

91-95.description: A pyramid with a 60-foot-square base bursts upward. Inside is a burial chamber containing a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.actors.Actor.t8WYD7ak07X7xpx8]{Mummy} , a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.actors.Actor.UFW8M3JHzHkxUEGM]{Mummy Lord} , or some other Undead of the DM’s choice. Its sarcophagus contains treasure of the DM’s choice.

96-100.description: A giant beanstalk sprouts, growing to a height of the DM’s choice. The top leads where the DM chooses, such as to a great view, a cloud giant’s castle, or another plane of existence.

2-2.description: Crumbling. Areas within the dungeon section are choked with rubble and have a 50 percent chance of being &Reference[Difficult Terrain]. &Reference[Half Cover] and hiding places are plentiful.

3-3.description: Neglected. One dungeon hazard—such as brown mold, green slime, or yellow mold (see @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgDmsToolbox000.JournalEntryPage.lVkdQivhFHqVmxg7]{Hazards})—is abundant.

4-4.description: Abandoned. Most of the dungeon is deserted. Dexterity (Stealth) checks have Disadvantage because any sounds stand out as unusual.

5-5.description: Secure. Ability checks made to break down doors, open locks, or carry out similar activities have Disadvantage.

6-6.description: Thriving. The dungeon is heavily populated. Any loud noises draw the attention of nearby creatures.

1-2.description: Abandoned after internal strife devastated its population

3-4.description: Abandoned because the site was cursed by a god or other powerful entity

5-6.description: Abandoned by its original creators when a plague spread through the dungeon

7-9.description: Amazingly well preserved ancient city inside a dome encased in volcanic ash, submerged underwater, or entombed in desert sands

10-12.description: Built as a fortress guarding a mountain pass

13-15.description: Built as a maze, either to protect treasure from intruders or as a gauntlet where prisoners were hunted by monsters

16-18.description: Built as a stronghold but abandoned after it fell to invaders

19-21.description: Built as a treasure vault to protect powerful magic items and great wealth

24-26.description: Built beneath a city in catacombs or sewers

27-29.description: Built beneath or on top of a mesa or several connected mesas

30-32.description: Built by a religious group to serve as a temple and linked to the energy of other planes of existence

33-35.description: Built by dwarves and decorated with enormous dwarven faces that have been defaced by its current inhabitants

39-40.description: Built in or among the branches of a tree

41-43.description: Built to house a planar portal but abandoned when creatures or energy from the other side of the portal seeped into the dungeon

44-46.description: Carved into a meteorite (before or after it fell to earth)

50-52.description: Caverns carved by a beholder’s disintegration eye ray, with unnaturally smooth walls and vertical shafts connecting different levels

53-55.description: Contains something that led to the downfall of its creators or inhabitants

56-58.description: Dug as a burrow by a monster that might still live inside

65-66.description: Intended as a death trap to eliminate any creature that enters, perhaps to guard a treasure or to harvest souls for a necromantic rite

70-72.description: Long known as the site of a great miracle or another auspicious event

73-75.description: Made by amphibious creatures (such as kuo-toa or aboleths), using water to protect the innermost reaches from air-breathing intruders

76-78.description: Made by a powerful spellcaster (perhaps a lich) as a site for magical research and experimentation

79-81.description: Made by giants at a vast scale

82-84.description: Natural caverns featuring a range of strikingly beautiful rock and crystal formations

85-87.description: On an island in an underground sea

88-90.description: On the back of a Gargantuan creature

91-93.description: Originally constructed as a mine but abandoned when tunnels connected to dangerous Underdark tunnels

94-96.description: Secreted away in a demiplane or in a pocket dimension

97-98.description: Slowly abandoned as its creators died out or migrated away

99-100.description: Transformed by multiple events or disasters over the course of centuries

1-1.description: The guest is an individual of great renown who stays for 7 days. At the end of their stay, the guest gives you a letter of recommendation (see @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgDmsToolbox000.JournalEntryPage.XpmEG4yalu71L9ed]{Marks of Prestige}).

2-2.description: The guest requests sanctuary while avoiding persecution for their beliefs or crimes. They depart 7 days later, but not before offering you a gift of [[/award 1d6*100gp]].

3-3.description: The guest is a mercenary, giving you one additional Bastion Defender. The guest doesn’t require a facility to house them, and they stay until you send them away or they’re killed.

4-4.description: The guest is a Friendly monster, such as a brass dragon or a treant. If your Bastion is attacked while this monster is your guest, it defends your Bastion, and you lose no Bastion Defenders. The monster leaves after it defends your Bastion once or when you send it away.

51-55.description: You have the &Reference[Stunned] condition until the end of your next turn, believing something awesome just happened.

56-60.description: A harmless swarm of butterflies fills a 10-foot Cube within 30 feet of yourself. The swarm disperses after 1 minute.

61-65.description: You pull a nonmagical object out of the hat. Roll [[/r 1d4]] to determine the object: on a 1, a vial of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagAcid0000000]{Acid}; on a 2, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagAlchemistsF]{flask of Alchemist’s Fire}; on a 3, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagCrowbar0000]{Crowbar}; on a 4, a lit @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagTorch000000]{Torch}.

66-70.description: You suffer a bout of “magic sickness” and have the &Reference[Poisoned] condition for 1 hour.

71-75.description: You have the &Reference[Petrified] condition until the end of your next turn.

76-80.description: You pull a nonmagical object out of the hat. Roll [[/r 1d4]] to determine the object: on a 1, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbwepDagger0000]{Dagger}; on a 2, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagRope0000000]{Rope} with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagGrapplingHo]{Grappling Hook} tied to one end; on a 3, a bag of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagCaltrops000]{Caltrops}; on a 4, a gem worth 50 GP.

81-85.description: A creature appears in an unoccupied space as close to you as possible. The creature isn’t under your control and acts as it normally would, and it disappears after 1 hour or when it drops to 0 Hit Points. Roll [[/r 1d4]] to determine the creature: on a 1, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.actors.Actor.phbmobCamel00000]{Camel}; on a 2, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.actors.Actor.phbmobConstricto]{Constrictor Snake}; on a 3, an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.actors.Actor.phbmobElephant00]{Elephant}; on a 4, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.actors.Actor.phbmobMule000000]{Mule}.

86-90.description: A Hostile @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.actors.Actor.PcZ0QjIG6bHpffp9]{Swarm of Bats} flies out of the hat, occupies your space, and attacks you.

91-95.description: A vertical, 10-foot-diameter, two-way portal to another plane of existence opens in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you and remains open until the end of your next turn. The DM determines where it leads.

96-100.description: You pull a magic item out of the hat. Roll [[/r 1d6]] to determine the item’s rarity: on a 1–3, Common; on a 4–5, Uncommon; on a 6, Rare. The DM chooses the item, which disappears after 1 hour if it’s not consumed or destroyed before then.

1-1.description: Aberration. The item is ancient. At a glance, it seems to be covered with mucus.

2-2.description: Celestial. The item is half the normal weight and inscribed with feathered wings, suns, and stars. Fiends find it repulsive.

3-3.description: Devotees of Lolth. The item is half the normal weight. It is inscribed with spiders and webs in honor of Lolth.

4-4.description: Dragon. This item incorporates precious metals and gems from a dragon’s hoard. It grows warm when within 120 feet of a Dragon.

5-6.description: Dwarf. The item is durable and has Dwarvish runes worked into its design. It might be associated with a clan that would like to see it returned to their ancestral halls.

7-7.description: Elemental Air. The item is half the normal weight and feels hollow. If it’s made of fabric, it is diaphanous.

8-8.description: Elemental Earth. This item might be crafted from stone. Any cloth or leather elements are studded with finely polished rock.

9-9.description: Elemental Fire. This item is warm to the touch, and any metal parts are crafted from black iron. Flame imagery covers its surface.

10-10.description: Elemental Water. Lustrous fish scales replace leather or cloth on this item, and seashells and worked coral (as hard as any metal) replace metal portions.

11-12.description: Elf. The item is half the normal weight. It is adorned with symbols of nature: leaves, vines, stars, and the like.

13-13.description: Fey. The item is exquisitely crafted from the finest materials and glows with a pale radiance in moonlight, shedding Dim Light in a 5-foot radius. Any metal in the item is silver or mithral rather than iron or steel.

14-14.description: Fiend. The item is made of iron or horn, and any cloth or leather components are crafted from the hide of Fiends. Leering faces or vile runes are engraved on its surface. Celestials find it repulsive.

15-15.description: Giant. The item is larger than normal and was crafted by Giants for use by their smaller allies.

16-16.description: Gnome. The item is crafted to appear ordinary and well used. It could also incorporate gears and mechanical components, even if these aren’t essential to its function.

17-19.description: Human. The item was created during the heyday of a fallen human kingdom, or it is tied to a human of legend. It might hold writing in a forgotten language or symbols whose significance is lost to the ages.

20-20.description: Undead. The item incorporates symbols of death, such as bones and skulls, and it might be crafted from parts of corpses. It feels cold to the touch.

1-1.description: Arcane. This item was created for an ancient order of spellcasters and bears the order’s symbol.

2-2.description: Bane. This item was created to oppose creatures of a particular type, such as Aberrations or Dragons.

3-3.description: Heroic. A great hero once wielded this item. Anyone who knows the item’s history expects great deeds from the new owner.

4-4.description: Ornament. The item honors a special event. Inset gemstones, gold or platinum inlays, and gold or silver filigree adorn its surface.

5-5.description: Prophecy. The item features in a prophecy: its bearer is destined to play a key role in future events.

6-6.description: Religious. This item was used in religious ceremonies dedicated to a particular deity. It has religious symbols worked into it.

7-7.description: Sinister. This item is linked to a deed of great evil, such as a massacre or an assassination. It might have a name or be closely associated with a villain who used it.

8-8.description: Symbol of Power. This item was once used as part of royal regalia or as a badge of high office.

1-2.description: Beacon. You can take a Bonus Action to cause the item to shed Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet, or to extinguish the light.

3-3.description: Compass. You can take a Magic action to learn which way is magnetic north. Nothing happens if this property is used in a location that has no magnetic north.

4-4.description: Delver. While underground, you always know the item’s depth below the surface and the direction to the nearest staircase, ramp, or other path leading upward.

5-6.description: Guardian. The item warns you, granting a +2 bonus to your Initiative rolls if you don’t have the Incapacitated condition.

7-8.description: Harmonious. Attuning to this item takes only 1 minute.

9-9.description: Key. The item is used to unlock a container, chamber, vault, or door.

10-10.description: Secret Message. A message is hidden somewhere on the item. It might be visible only at a certain time, under the light of one phase of the moon, or in a specific location.

11-12.description: Sentinel. The DM chooses a kind of creature, such as mind flayers or trolls. This item glows faintly when such creatures are within 120 feet of it.

13-13.description: Songcraft. Whenever this item is struck or is used to strike a foe, you hear a fragment of an ancient song.

14-15.description: Strange Material. The item was created from a material that is bizarre given its purpose. Its durability is unaffected.

16-16.description: Temperate. You are unharmed by temperatures of 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower, and 100 degrees Fahrenheit or higher.

17-17.description: Unbreakable. The item can’t be broken. Special means must be used to destroy it.

18-18.description: War Leader. You can take a Magic action to cause your voice or signal to carry clearly for up to 600 feet until the end of your next turn.

19-19.description: Waterborne. This item floats on water and other liquids. You have Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to swim.

1-1.description: Blissful. You feel fortunate and optimistic about what the future holds. Butterflies and other harmless creatures might frolic in the item’s presence.

2-2.description: Confident. The item helps you feel self-assured.

3-3.description: Covetous. You become obsessed with material wealth.

4-4.description: Fragile. The item crumbles, frays, chips, or cracks slightly when wielded, worn, or activated. This quirk has no effect on its properties.

5-5.description: Loud. The item makes a loud noise—such as a clang, a shout, or a resonating gong—when used.

6-6.description: Metamorphic. The item periodically alters its appearance in slight ways. You have no control over these minor alterations, which have no effect on the item’s use.

7-7.description: Painful. You experience a harmless flash of pain when using the item.

8-8.description: Repulsive. You feel a sense of distaste when in contact with the item and continue to experience discomfort while bearing it.

1-20.description: While attuned to the Artifact, one of your ability scores (DM’s choice) increases by 2, to a maximum of 24.

21-30.description: While attuned to the Artifact, you regain 1d6 Hit Points at the start of each of your turns if you have at least 1 Hit Point.

31-40.description: When you hit with an attack roll while attuned to the Artifact, the target takes an extra 1d6 Force damage.

41-50.description: While you’re attuned to the Artifact, your Speed increases by 10 feet.

51-60.description: While attuned to the Artifact, you can cast one level 4 spell (chosen by the DM) from it. After you cast the spell, roll 1d6. On a roll of 1–5, you can’t cast it again in this way until the next dawn.

61-70.description: As 51–60 above, except the spell is level 5.

71-80.description: As 51–60 above, except the spell is level 6.

81-90.description: As 51–60 above, except the spell is level 7.

91-100.description: While attuned to the Artifact, you have Immunity to the Blinded, Deafened, Petrified, and Stunned conditions.

1-9.description: You can’t attune to other magic items while you’re attuned to the Artifact. When you become attuned to the Artifact, your Attunement to other magic items ends immediately.

10-18.description: When you become attuned to the Artifact, a random one of your ability scores is reduced by 2, to a minimum of 3. A Greater Restoration spell restores the ability.

19-27.description: When you become attuned to the Artifact, you take 8d10 Psychic damage.

28-36.description: The first time you become attuned to the Artifact, it gives you a quest determined by the DM. You can’t use any of the Artifact’s properties until you complete the quest.

37-45.description: Each time you become attuned to the Artifact, there is a 10 percent chance that you attract the attention of a god who sends an avatar to wrest the Artifact from you. The avatar has the same alignment as its creator and uses the Empyrean stat block. Once it obtains the Artifact, the avatar vanishes.

46-54.description: Each time you become attuned to the Artifact, you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or die from the shock. If you die, you’re instantly transformed into a Wight under the DM’s control that must protect the Artifact.

55-63.description: The Artifact dilutes potions within 10 feet of itself, rendering them nonmagical.

64-72.description: The Artifact erases scrolls within 10 feet of itself, rendering them nonmagical.

73-81.description: While you’re attuned to the Artifact, creatures of a particular type other than Humanoid (chosen by the DM) are always Hostile toward you.

82-90.description: While attuned to the Artifact, you have Vulnerability to all damage.

91-96.description: The Artifact imprisons a Death Slaad. Each time you become attuned to the Artifact, the slaad has a 10 percent chance of escaping, whereupon it appears in an unoccupied space as close to you as possible and attacks you.

97-100.description: While attuned to the Artifact, you can’t spend Hit Point Dice or regain Hit Points.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgMoonblade0000.ActiveEffect.o2IcKz2aAooQr7EK]

61-75.description:
@UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgMoonblade0000.ActiveEffect.vwQstbhAl6CdxUeN]
When you hit with an attack roll using the Moonblade , you deal an extra 1d6 Force damage. Each time the weapon gains this property after the first, the extra damage increases by 1d6, to a maximum of 3d6. Reroll if the Moonblade already deals an extra 3d6 Force damage on a hit.

81-85.description:
@UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgMoonblade0000.ActiveEffect.VC3o2KY4btBnaIAc]
The Moonblade scores a &Reference[CriticalHits]{Critical Hit} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

86-95.description:
@UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgMoonblade0000.ActiveEffect.rzsbnjT5QiK2Jq8E]
You can take a Bonus Action to cause the Moonblade to flash brightly. Each other creature that is within 30 feet of you and not behind Total Cover must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have the Blinded condition for 1 minute. A creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. You can’t use this property again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

96-99.description:
@UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgMoonblade0000.ActiveEffect.vZ0T3fFRBE3NHG6o]

100-100.description:
@UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgMoonblade0000.ActiveEffect.Qzkx9WVqILq2hG5c]
You can take a Magic action to conjure a spectral entity that resembles a shadowy elf if you don’t already have one serving you. The entity appears in an unoccupied space within 120 feet of you. It uses the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.actors.Actor.QGcQYZbVl4bWzi4E]{Shadow} stat block with these changes: it is a Fey, has a Neutral alignment, and doesn’t create new shadows. You control this entity, deciding how it acts and moves. It remains until it drops to 0 Hit Points or you dismiss it as a Magic action.

3-3.description: The NPC (or their family) has been threatened with harm unless the NPC does something.

1-1.description: A town crier announces that someone is hoping to hire adventurers.

2-2.description: Someone the characters want to impress or need a favor from asks them to deal with the adventure situation.

3-3.description: When the characters arrive in a new city, they find a job board where someone has posted in search of adventurers.

4-4.description: A wealthy patron who is aware of the adventurers’ accomplishments writes to them, offering to pay them for their talents.

5-5.description: A citizen in need, who has learned of the adventurers’ accomplishments and kindness, travels miles to find them and implore them for help.

6-6.description: The adventurers are arrested (on valid or invented charges) and offered a chance to escape punishment by completing a quest.

1-1.description: When magic fails to revive a dead person, the only solution is to venture to the Outer Planes to find the person’s spirit and either release it from some prison or convince the person to return to life.

2-2.description: People who venture into the woods keep accidentally wandering into the Feywild or the Shadowfell. They might never return, return with no sense of how much time has passed, or return dramatically changed.

3-3.description: A long-dead oracle is the only one who knows how a terrible prophecy might be averted, but the cataclysmic fulfillment of the prophecy has already begun.

4-4.description: A god has stopped answering prayers and won’t respond to any Commune spell.

5-5.description: A devil has tricked an angel into meddling in the Blood War, and the angel seeks mortal aid.

6-6.description: A ancestor of one of the characters must be convinced to bless the character before the full power of the character’s bloodline can be unleashed.

7-7.description: A foolhardy knight carried a holy weapon on a doomed mission into the Nine Hells, and the powers of Mount Celestia want the weapon and the knight’s remains retrieved.

8-8.description: A titan is imprisoned on an Outer Plane. The characters might be trying to stop those who seek to release it, or they might want to release it to help defend the world from a greater threat.

9-9.description: To prove themselves worthy of an even greater quest, the characters are sent to slay a horrible monster, win the favor of a powerful planar being, negotiate peace between two warring planar factions, or retrieve a long-lost item on another plane.

10-10.description: An item of legend is being sold at auction in Sigil, the City of Brass, or some other planar metropolis.

1-1.description: Both potions lose their effects, and the mixture creates a magical explosion in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on itself. Each creature in that area takes [[/damage 4d10 type=force]] damage.

2-8.description: Both potions lose their effects, and the mixture becomes an ingested poison of your choice (see @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgDmsToolbox000.JournalEntryPage.UfAEdm3LbTzvQHC5]{Poison}).

26-35.description: Both potions work, but with their numerical effects and durations halved. If a potion has no numerical effect and no duration, it instead loses its effect.

91-99.description: Both potions work, but the numerical effects and duration of one potion are doubled. If neither potion has anything to double in this way, they work normally.

100-100.description: Only one potion works, but its effects are permanent. Choose the simplest effect to make permanent or the one that seems the most fun. For example, a Potion of Healing might increase the drinker’s Hit Point maximum by [[/roll 2d4 + 2]], or a Potion of Invisibility might give the drinker the Invisible condition indefinitely. At your discretion, a Dispel Magic spell or similar magic might end this lasting effect.

1-1.description: A cart or another large obstacle blocks your way. Make a [[/save dex dc=10]] saving throw to get past the obstacle. On a failed save, the obstacle counts as 10 feet of &Reference[Difficult Terrain] for you.

2-2.description: A crowd blocks your way. Make a [[/save str dc=10]], [[/save dex dc=10]], or [[/save cha dc=10]] saving throw (your choice) to navigate through the crowd. On a failed save, the crowd counts as 10 feet of &Reference[Difficult Terrain] for you.

3-3.description: A maze of barrels, crates, or similar obstacles stands in your way. Make a [[/save dex dc=10]] or [[/save int dc=10]] saving throw (your choice) to navigate the maze. On a failed save, the maze counts as 10 feet of &Reference[Difficult Terrain] for you.

4-4.description: The ground is slippery with rain, spilled oil, or some other liquid. Make a [[/save dex dc=10]] saving throw. On a failed save, you have the &Reference[Prone] condition.

5-5.description: You encounter a brawl in progress. Make a [[/save str dc=15]], [[/save dex dc=15]], or [[/save cha dc=15]] saving throw (your choice) to get past the brawlers unimpeded. On a failed save, you take [[/damage 2d4 type=bludgeoning]] damage, and the brawlers count as 10 feet of &Reference[Difficult Terrain] for you.

6-6.description: You must make a sharp turn to avoid colliding with something impassable. Make a [[/save dex dc=10]] saving throw to navigate the turn. On a failed save, you collide with something hard and take [[/damage 1d4 type=bludgeoning]] damage.

1-20.description: You cast a spell originating from the chosen point. Roll 1d10 to determine the spell: on a 1–2, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDarkness00]{Darkness}; on a 3–4, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplFaerieFire]{Faerie Fire}; on a 5–6, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplFireball00]{Fireball}; on a 7–8, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSlow000000]{Slow}; on a 9–10, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplStinkingCl]{Stinking Cloud}.

21-25.description: Nothing happens at the chosen point of origin. Instead, you have the &Reference[Stunned] condition until the start of your next turn, believing something awesome just happened.

26-30.description: You cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplGustofWind]{Gust of Wind}. The Line created by the spell extends from you to the chosen point of origin.

31-35.description: Nothing happens at the chosen point of origin. Instead, you take [[/damage 1d6 type=psychic]] damage.

36-40.description: Heavy rain falls for 1 minute in a 120-foot-high, 60-foot-radius Cylinder centered on the chosen point of origin. During that time, the area of effect is &Reference[Lightly Obscured].

41-45.description: A cloud of 600 oversized butterflies fills a 60-foot-high, 30-foot-radius Cylinder centered on the chosen point of origin. The butterflies remain for 10 minutes, during which time the area of effect is &Reference[Heavily Obscured].

46-50.description: You cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLightningB]{Lightning Bolt}. The Line created by the spell extends from you to the chosen point of origin.

51-55.description: The creature closest to the chosen point of origin is enlarged as if you had cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEnlargeRed]{Enlarge/Reduce} on it. If the target isn’t you and can’t be affected by that spell, you become the target instead.

56-60.description: A magically formed creature appears in an unoccupied space as close to the chosen point of origin as possible. The creature isn’t under your control, acts as it normally would, and disappears after 1 hour or when it drops to 0 Hit Points. Roll [[/r 1d4]] to determine which creature appears. On a 1, a Rhinoceros appears; on a 2, an Elephant appears; and on a 3–4, a Rat appears.

61-64.description: Grass covers a 60-foot-radius circle of ground, with the center of that circle as close to the chosen point of origin as possible. Grass that’s already there grows to ten times its normal size and remains overgrown for 1 minute.

65-68.description: An object of the DM’s choice disappears into the Ethereal Plane. The object must be neither worn nor carried, within 120 feet of the chosen point of origin, and no larger than 10 feet in any dimension. If there are no such objects in range, nothing happens.

69-72.description: Nothing happens at the chosen point of origin. Instead, you shrink as if you had cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEnlargeRed]{Enlarge/Reduce} on yourself and remain in that state for 1 minute.

73-77.description: Leaves grow from the creature nearest to the chosen point of origin. Unless they are picked off, the leaves turn brown and fall off after 24 hours.

78-82.description: Nothing happens at the chosen point of origin. Instead, a burst of colorful, shimmering light extends from you in a 30-foot Emanation. Each creature in the area must succeed on a [[/save con 15]] saving throw or have the &Reference[Blinded] condition for 1 minute. A creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

83-87.description: Nothing happens at the chosen point of origin. Instead, you cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplInvisibili]{Invisibility} on yourself.

88-92.description: Nothing happens at the chosen point of origin. Instead, a stream of [[/r 1d4*10 #Gems]] gems, each worth 1 GP, shoots from the wand’s tip in a Line 30 feet long and 5 feet wide toward the chosen point of origin. Each gem deals [[/damage 1 type=bludgeoning]] damage, and the total damage of the gems is divided equally among all creatures in the Line.

93-97.description: You cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplPolymorph0]{Polymorph}, targeting the creature closest to the chosen point of origin. Roll [[/r 1d4]] to determine the target’s new form. On a 1, the new form is a Black Bear; on a 2, the new form is a Giant Wasp; on a 3–4, the new form is a Frog.

98-100.description: The creature closest to the chosen point of origin makes a [[/save con 15]] saving throw. On a failed save, the creature has the &Reference[Restrained] condition and begins to turn to stone. While Restrained in this way, the creature repeats the save at the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the effect ends. On a failed save, the creature has the &Reference[Petrified] condition instead of the Restrained condition. The petrification lasts until the creature is freed by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplGreaterRes]{Greater Restoration} spell or similar magic.

1-4.description: Roll on this table at the start of each of your turns for the next minute, ignoring this result on subsequent rolls.

5-8.description: A creature that is Friendly toward you appears in a random unoccupied space within 60 feet of you. The creature is under the DM’s control and disappears 1 minute later. Roll [[/r 1d4]] to determine the creature: on a 1, a Modron Duodrone appears; on a 2, a Flumph appears; on a 3, a Modron Monodrone appears; on a 4, a Unicorn appears. See the Monster Manual for the creature’s stat block.

9-12.description: For the next minute, you regain 5 Hit Points at the start of each of your turns.

13-16.description: Creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws against the next spell you cast in the next minute that involves a saving throw.

17-20.description: You are subjected to an effect that lasts for 1 minute unless its description says otherwise. Roll [[/r 1d8]] to determine the effect: on a 1, you’re surrounded by faint, ethereal music only you and creatures within 5 feet of you can hear; on a 2, your size increases by one size category; on a 3, you grow a long beard made of feathers that remains until you sneeze, at which point the feathers explode from your face and vanish; on a 4, you must shout when you speak; on a 5, illusory butterflies flutter in the air within 10 feet of you; on a 6, an eye appears on your forehead, granting you Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks; on an 7, pink bubbles float out of your mouth whenever you speak; on an 8, your skin turns a vibrant shade of blue for 24 hours or until the effect is ended by a Remove Curse spell.

21-24.description: For the next minute, all your spells with a casting time of an action have a casting time of a Bonus Action.

25-28.description: You are transported to the Astral Plane until the end of your next turn. You then return to the space you previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

29-32.description: The next time you cast a spell that deals damage within the next minute, don’t roll the spell’s damage dice for the damage. Instead use the highest number possible for each damage die.

33-36.description: You have Resistance to all damage for the next minute.

37-40.description: You turn into a potted plant until the start of your next turn. While you’re a plant, you have the &Reference[Incapacitated] condition and have Vulnerability to all damage. If you drop to 0 Hit Points, your pot breaks, and your form reverts.

41-44.description: For the next minute, you can teleport up to 20 feet as a Bonus Action on each of your turns.

45-48.description: You and up to three creatures you choose within 30 feet of you have the Invisible condition for 1 minute. This invisibility ends on a creature immediately after it makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.

49-52.description: A spectral shield hovers near you for the next minute, granting you a +2 bonus to AC and immunity to Magic Missile.

53-56.description: You can take one extra action on this turn.

57-60.description: You cast a random spell. If the spell normally requires Concentration, it doesn’t require Concentration in this case; the spell lasts for its full duration. Roll [[/r 1d10]] to determine the spell: on a 1, Confusion; on a 2, Fireball; on a 3, Fog Cloud; on a 4, Fly (cast on a random creature within 60 feet of you), on a 5, Grease; on a 6, Levitate (cast on yourself); on a 7, Magic Missile (cast as a level 5 spell); on an 8, Mirror Image; on a 9, Polymorph (cast on yourself), and if you fail the saving throw, you turn into a Goat (see appendix B); on a 10, See Invisibility.

61-64.description: For the next minute, any flammable, nonmagical object you touch that isn’t being worn or carried by another creature bursts into flame, takes 1d4 Fire damage, and is burning.

65-68.description: If you die within the next hour, you immediately revive as if by the Reincarnate spell.

69-72.description: You have the &Reference[Frightened] condition until the end of your next turn. The DM determines the source of your fear.

73-76.description: You teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

77-80.description: A random creature within 60 feet of you has the Poisoned condition for [[/r 1d4]] hours.

81-84.description: You radiate Bright Light in a 30-foot radius for the next minute. Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of you has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.

85-88.description: Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you take [[/damage 1d10 type=necrotic]] damage. You regain Hit Points equal to the sum of the Necrotic damage dealt.

89-92.description: Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you take [[/damage 4d10 type=lightning]] damage.

93-96.description: You and all creatures within 30 feet of you have Vulnerability to Piercing damage for the next minute.

97-100.description: Roll [[/r 1d6]]: On a 1, you regain [[/healing 2d10]]{2d10} Hit Points; on a 2, one ally of your choice within 300 feet of you regains [[/healing 2d10]]{2d10} Hit Points; on a 3, you regain your lowest-level expended spell slot; on a 4, one ally of your choice within 300 feet of you regains their lowest-level expended spell slot; on a 5, you regain all your expended Sorcery Points; on a 6, all the effects of row 17–20 affect you simultaneously.
